eu-ai-act: The EU's horizontal, risk-tiered law (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by the Digital Omnibus); high-risk Annex III obligations apply from 2 December 2027 and GPAI obligations have applied since 2 August 2025.
iso-42001: The AI management-system (AIMS) standard whose Annex A groups control objectives into nine areas (A.2–A.10); a management-system standard, not the Article 17 QMS, and its European adoption confers no presumption of conformity.
nist-rmf: The voluntary NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0, organising risk work into four functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) that map cleanly onto the five-layer stack.
crosswalk: The reverse index that names, for each obligation, the engineering artefact that produces its evidence and the stack layer the artefact lives in, maintained as a machine-readable file emitted as OSCAL component definitions.
l1: Layer 01 Govern-as-Code: policy-as-code and QMS-as-code answering obligations such as EU AI Act Art. 9 (risk management) and Art. 17 (quality management system).
l2: Layer 02 Inventory & Transparency: the registry, AIBOM and model/data cards answering technical-documentation, registration and transparency obligations (Art. 11, Art. 49/71, Art. 50).
l3: Layer 03 Evals & Red Teaming as Evidence: the eval gate and adversarial red-team suite answering accuracy, robustness and GPAI systemic-risk evaluation obligations (Art. 15, Art. 55).
l4: Layer 04 Runtime Controls & Observability: guardrails, human oversight, kill switch and logging answering human-oversight, logging and content-marking obligations (Art. 12, Art. 14, Art. 50).
l5: Layer 05 Assurance & Continuous Compliance: the live assurance store any lower layer writes into, meeting post-market monitoring and serious-incident-reporting obligations (Art. 72, Art. 73).
evidence: Machine-readable evidence emitted continuously as OSCAL and signed logs, turning the audit question into a query against the crosswalk rather than a hunt through a wiki.
